COURT’S OR JUDGES’S ORDERS
WPMS No. 1523 of 2023
Hon’ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J.
Mr. Siddhartha Singh, learned counsel for the 
petitioners.
Mr. Piyush Garg, learned counsel for the 
contesting respondent no. 1.
Mr. N.S. Pundir, learned Deputy Advocate 
General and Mr. M.S. Bisht, Brief Holder for the 
State/respondent no. 2 to 4.
Respondent nos. 5 to 8 are the 
plaintiffs/proforma respondents.
By the present writ petition, the petitioners
are praying for the following reliefs:-
“(i) Issue a writ, order or direction, in the nature of 
certiorari calling for the record of the case and quash 
the impugned judgment dated 08.05.2023 (Annexure 
No. 2) passed by Learned Board of Revenue 
Uttarakhand, Dehradun in Revision No. 136 of 2014 
– 15 Ramesh Chand Vs. Jodha Ram and Others.”
Mr. Piyush Garg, learned counsel for the 
respondent no. 1 submits that the defendant no. 1 
has already filed the written statement in 
compliance to the order passed by the Board of 
Revenue dated 08.05.2023, which has been taken 
on record by order dated 15.06.2023 and in 
reference to this, he placed before this Court the  certified copy of the order dated 15.06.2023 passed 
by the Assistant Collector, 1st Class, Kaladhungi, 
District Nainital in Revenue Case No. 22/107 of 
1985-1986.
Mr. Siddhartha Singh, learned counsel for the 
petitioners submits that let the suit be proceeded on 
the basis of the written statement filed by the 
defendant no. 1. However, the respondents should 
pay a cost for this and the suit be expedited on day 
to day hearing basis.
In view of such submissions, as advanced by 
learned counsel for the petitioners, which has not 
been opposed by the learned counsel for the 
respondents, let the Assistant Collector, 1st Class, 
Kaladhungi, District Nainital may proceed to 
expedite the Revenue Case No. 22/107 of 1985-
1986 by day to day hearing basis, within a period of 
two months from the date of production of certified 
copy of this order.
The respondents shall also pay a cost of Rs. 
10,000/- to the petitioners, within a period of one 
week from today.
It is made clear that the Assistant Collector, 
1
st Class, Kaladhungi, District Nainital will not give 
adjournment to either of the parties to the suit in 
question.
The present writ petition is being kept  pending and the Assistant Collector, 1st Class, 
Kaladhungi, District Nainital is requested to place 
before this Court the status of the case on the date 
fixed.
List this matter on 25.08.2023.
Let a certified copy of this order be supplied 
to learned counsels for the parties, within 24 hours, 
on payment of usual charges.
 
(Rakesh Thapliyal, J.)
 21.06.2023
Ujjwal

COURT’S OR JUDGE’S ORDERS 
 MCC No. 2/2023 (For Review Application) 
In 
WPMS No. 1523 of 2023 
Hon’ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J.
1. Mr. Siddhartha Singh, learned counsel for 
the petitioners. 
2. Mr. Piyush Garg, learned counsel for 
respondent no. 1. 
3. Mr. N.S. Pundir, learned Deputy Advocate 
General for the State/respondent nos. 2 and 4. 
4. The present review application (MCC No. 
2/2023) has been filed for reviewing the judgment 
and order dated 21.06.2023. In paragraph-7 of the 
affidavit filed in support of review application, it 
is contended that on 21.06.2023 the petitioners 
could not come personally and had not instructed 
the counsel to make such concession. 
5. It is further contended by the petitioner that 
he want to contest the petition on merits, as he is 
facing irreparable loss due to the concession got 
recorded by the counsel which was beyond any 
authority or any instruction. 
6. Today, the petitioner no. 1 Mr. Jodha Ram, 
who is aged about 94 years and petitioner no. 2/2 
Mr. Nand Lal S/o Late Kundan Ram are present 
in the court and they are duly identified by their 
counsel through their Aadhar Cards. 
7. Since, the order dated 21.06.2023 was a 
consenting order; however, today, the petitioner 
no. 1, who is aged about 94 years submits that he 
wants to contest this writ petition on merit, for 
which the counsel for the respondent has no 
objection. In view of this, review application is 
allowed. Order dated 21.06.2023 is recalled. 
8. The cheque of Rs. 10,000/-, which was  ordered to be paid while passing the order dated 
21.06.2023, is returned by Mr. Jodha Ram to the 
counsel for the respondent. 
9. Learned counsel for the petitioners Mr. 
Siddhartha Singh submits that due to the conduct 
of his client, he wants to withdraw his 
vakalatnama.
10. In view of this, learned counsel for the 
petitioners Mr. Siddhartha Singh is permitted to 
withdraw his vakalatnama. The petitioner no. 1, 
who is present in the Court is permitted to engage 
some other counsel. 
11. List this matter after one week. 
 
 (Rakesh Thapliyal, J.) 
 19.07.2023

IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND 
AT NAINITAL
SRI JUSTICE RAKESH THAPLIYAL, J. 
Dated: July 27, 2023 
WRIT PETITION (M/S) No. 1523 OF 2023
Between: 
Jodha Ram and others. …..…….Petitioners.
And 
Charandas and others. ….…Respondents.
Counsel for the petitioners: Mr. T.A Khan, Sr. Advocate, assisted 
Mohd. Saifi, Advocate for the 
petitioners. 
Counsel for the respondents: Mr. Piyush Garg, learned counsel for 
the respondent no. 1.
Mr. Sushil Vashisht, learned Standing 
Counsel with Mr. M.S. Bisht, learned 
Brief Holder for the State/ 
respondents no. 2 and 4. 
Upon hearing the learned Counsel, the Court made the following Order: 
(per Sri Rakesh Thapliyal, J.)
1. Shri T.A. Khan, Sr. Advocate, for the petitioners, will 
supply a copy of the writ petition to Ms. Anjali Bhargava, counsel 
for respondent no. 3 – Gram Sabha. 
2. Since respondents no. 5 – 8 are pro forma respondents, 
therefore, at this stage, there is no need to issue notice to them.
3. Petitioners – plaintiffs filed a suit no. 22/107 of 1985 – 86 
under Section 229-B of the U.P.Z.A. & L.R. wherein on 26.06.1986
temporary injunction was granted and petitioners were also 
given exemption under Section 80 (2) of the CPC. This order 
dated 26.06.1986 was made absolute by the order dated 
05.11.1986 with a direction to the plaintiffs – petitioners to make 
Forest Department, defendant. Against the order dated 
05.11.1986, Z.A. Appeal No. 35 / 106 of 1986-87 was preferred 
before the Additional Commissioner (Judicial) and the Additional  2
Commissioner (Judicial) allowed the said appeal and set aside the 
order dated 05.11.1986 vide the order dated 10.12.1990. Against 
this order, plaintiffs – petitioners preferred Second Appeal No. 93 
of 1990-1991 before the Board of Revenue, which was dismissed 
on 11.07.1994. Thereafter, defendant no. 1 moved an application 
under Order 7 Rule 11 CPC, which was dismissed by the 
Assistant Collector vide order dated 19.01.2006, against which 
Z.A. Appeal No. 42 / 2005-06 was filed by defendant no. 1, which 
was also dismissed on 11.07.2007. Against this order dated 
11.07.2007, defendant no. 1 preferred a Revision No. 03 of 2007 
before the Additional Chief Revenue Commissioner, which was 
also dismissed on 25.07.2009. Thereafter, the defendant no. 1 
moved an application for adjournment on the ground that the 
plaintiffs filed a review application before the Board of Revenue 
which is pending, however, that application was rejected on 
15.04.2010 and by the same order the Assistant Collector closed 
the opportunity of defendant no. 1 to file written statement. 
Against this order dated 15.04.2010, defendant no. 1 filed Z.A. 
Appeal No. 31 / 2009-10 before the Commissioner, which was 
also dismissed on 14.02.2013. Then, Second Appeal No. 136 of 
2014-15 was preferred by defendant no. 1 before the Board of 
Revenue and the Board of Revenue vide order dated 26.05.2015 
directed to file written statement by 09.06.2015 and pursuant to 
the said order, written statement was filed by defendant no. 1. 
Against the order dated 26.05.2015, plaintiffs filed writ petition 
before this High Court being WPMS No. 1287 of 2015. The writ 
petition was allowed by the Coordinate Bench of this Court vide 
order dated 03.12.2021 and order of the Board of Revenue dated 
26.05.2021 was quashed, however, liberty was granted to 
defendant no. 1 to move an application for conversion of second 
appeal to revision and if such application is filed, the same shall  3
be considered as per law. Thereafter, application was moved and 
the second appeal was converted to revision no. 136/2014-2015. 
The Board of Revenue by order dated 08.05.2023 allowed the 
revision and set aside the order dated 14.02.2023 as well as order 
dated 15.04.2010 passed by the Assistant Collector, First Class. By 
this order the Board of Revenue granted an opportunity to file 
written statement by the next date and the trial court was 
directed to expedite the suit within a period of three months. 
4. Now being aggrieved by the order dated 08.05.2023 passed 
by the Board of Revenue, present writ petition has been preferred 
by the petitioner. 
5. Mr. Piyush Garg, counsel for the petitioner, submits that 
since by order dated 10.12.1990 passed by the Additional 
Commissioner, temporary injunction order dated 15.11.1986 was 
set aside whereby order granting temporary injunction dated 
26.08.1986 was made absolute and there was no exemption under 
Section 80 (2) CPC because once this order dated 15.11.1986 was 
set aside then whole order dated 26.08.1986 will go whereby 
exemption from 80 (2) as well as temporary injunction was 
granted. 
6. Mr. Piyush Garg, counsel for the petitioner, submits that 
after the order dated 10.12.1990, since the order granting 
exemption under Section 80 (2) CPC came to an end and, 
therefore, suit was not maintainable and that was the reason 
defendant moved an application under Order 7 Rule 11 CPC.
7. This submission is strongly opposed by Mr. T.A. Khan, Sr. 
Advocate, for the petitioner. 
8. For deciding the matter, version of the respondent no. 1 is 
required and only for that purpose, ten days’ time is granted to  4
the respondent no. 1 to file counter affidavit and thereafter, one 
week’s time is granted to the petitioner to file rejoinder affidavit, 
thereafter. 
9. List this case on 18.08.2023. 
10. Meanwhile further proceeding of case no. 22/107 of 1985-86 
pending in the Court of Assistant Collector, First Class, 
Kaladungi, is stayed till 18.08.2023. 
__________________ 
RAKESH THAPLIYAL, J.
SKS

COURT’S OR JUDGES’S ORDERS
WPMS No. 1523 of 2023
Hon’ble Vivek Bharti Sharma, J.
Present Mr. T. A. Khan, Senior Advocate 
assisted by Mr. Mohd. Shafy, counsel for the 
petitioners.
Present Mr. Piyush Garg, counsel for the 
respondent no. 1. 
Present Mr. Devesh Ghildiyal, Brief 
Holder for the State. 
Present Ms. Anjali Bhargawa, counsel 
for the respondent no. 3.
2. Counsel for the petitioners would submit 
that the petitioners had filed a Suit No. 22 of 
1985-86 before the Assistant Collector 1st
Class, Haldwani, District Nainital under 
Section 229-B of U.P. Zamindari Abolition 
and Land Reforms Act, 1950 for declaring 
their Bhoomidhari rights over the suit property 
wherein the status quo order was passed on 
26.08.1986; that, this order was confirmed by 
the Assistant Collector, Haldwani; that, feeling 
aggrieved by the said order, the respondents
preferred the Appeal before the Additional 
Commissioner, Kumaon Division; which was 
allowed and the interim order of status quo 
was set-aside; that, against the said order, the 
petitioners preferred the Second Appeal before 
the Board of Revenue, which was dismissed.
He would further submit that the last 
order came in the year 2006 despite the fact, 
that the respondents did not file written 
statement since 2006 to 2010, the opportunity 
to file written statement was closed by the trial 
court against which, the respondents went 
through several stages and finally by the  impugned order dated 08.05.2023 passed by 
the Board of Revenue Uttarakhand, Dehradun, 
an opportunity to file written statement was 
granted to the respondents, albeit, with the 
direction to the trial court to decide the suit 
within three months. Feeling aggrieved by the 
order dated 08.05.2023, the 
petitioners/plaintiffs preferred the present writ 
petition. 
3. Admit the petition. 
4. Pleadings have been exchanged. 
5. List this matter on 22.04.2024 for final 
hearing.
 (Vivek Bharti Sharma, J.) 
 28.11.2023
Akash
